root_cause.text: `hbh_mt6_check()` in the netfilter IPv6 hop-by-hop matcher failed to validate the user-supplied `optsnr` count against the fixed-size `struct ip6t_opts.opts[IP6T_OPTS_OPTSNR]` array, allowing oversized rule data to trigger an out-of-bounds array access during matching.
root_cause.evidence: The CVE says `struct ip6t_opts stores at most IP6T_OPTS_OPTSNR option descriptors, but hbh_mt6_check() does not reject larger optsnr values supplied from userspace`, and the patch adds `if (optsinfo->optsnr > IP6T_OPTS_OPTSNR) return -EINVAL;` to reject oversized counts; the reported UBSAN shows `index 16 is out of range for type '__u16 [16]'`, confirming the fixed 16-element array was exceeded.

intent_record.intent_summary: Add a bounds check to reject option lists that exceed the supported maximum.
intent_record.what: In hbh_mt6_check(), a new validation block was added after the unknown-flags check. It tests whether optsinfo->optsnr is greater than IP6T_OPTS_OPTSNR, prints a debug message if so, and returns -EINVAL.
intent_record.how: At runtime, rule-checking now rejects configurations that specify more supported options than the kernel code allows, preventing oversized/unsupported option counts from being accepted during matcher setup.

grouping_result.intent: Add a bounds check to reject option lists that exceed the supported maximum.

relevance_review.reason: The change adds a bounds check to reject oversized option lists, which directly addresses the root cause: failure to validate `optsnr` against the fixed-size `opts` array, leading to out-of-bounds access.

candidates.rationale: This is the pre-fix control-flow point where option parsing proceeds without any prior bounds validation of the user-supplied option count, allowing oversized rule data to reach later out-of-bounds accesses.

vuln_statements.explanation: This control-flow point begins option processing without any preceding validation of the user-supplied option count against the fixed-size opts[] array, which is the root cause that allows oversized rule data to later trigger an out-of-bounds access.

commit 8ca31ce52a5cfd03b960fd81a49197ae85d25347
Author: Yasuyuki Kozakai <yasuyuki.kozakai@toshiba.co.jp>

    netfilter: ip6t_{hbh,dst}: Rejects not-strict mode on rule insertion
    
    The current code ignores rules for internal options in HBH/DST options
    header in packet processing if 'Not strict' mode is specified (which is not
    implemented). Clearly it is not expected by user.
    
    Kernel should reject HBH/DST rule insertion with 'Not stri
bic_trace_step.reason: The shown function body for `hbh_mt6_check()` now rejects the problematic mode before rule acceptance: `if (optsinfo->flags & IP6T_OPTS_NSTRICT) { pr_debug("ip6t_opts: Not strict - not implemented"); return false; }`. The vulnerable root cause was failure to validate user-supplied option data against the fixed-size array during matching, but this snippet is a rule-insertion check and does not show any out-of-bounds access or an oversized `optsnr` use. Since the code now explicitly rejects the unsupported non-strict case at validation time, the fix is already present in this commit snippet.
